reviews.author: Vikram Rathore
reviews.title: ADAS features genuinely useful on the expressway
reviews.text: Lane-keep assist and adaptive cruise make the Delhi-Jaipur run far less tiring. Interiors feel a segment above for the price.

reviews.author: Priyanka Das
reviews.title: Best-selling for a reason, but rear diesel clatter is noticeable
reviews.text: Cabin is quiet at idle but the diesel gets a bit vocal under hard acceleration. Everything else — space, features, ride quality — is excellent.

spareParts.authorizedServiceNote: Hyundai's Blue Link connected service network covers most tier-1 and tier-2 cities; the Creta is the highest-stocked model at every outlet.
spareParts.tip: ADAS-related sensor work should only be done at authorised service — calibration equipment is not commonly available at independent garages.

faqs.q: Petrol or diesel — which is better for city + highway mix?
faqs.a: If annual running crosses 15,000-18,000 km with regular highway trips, diesel's efficiency edge pays back faster; otherwise the petrol IVT is smoother for city use.

reviews.author: Farhan Sheikh
reviews.title: Turbo DCT is a genuine hot-hatch feel
reviews.text: The 1.0 turbo with DCT is surprisingly quick and refined for the segment. Ride is on the firmer side, which some buyers may not expect from a hatchback.

spareParts.authorizedServiceNote: Standard Hyundai network pricing; turbo-DCT variants require dealer-level diagnostic tools for the transmission.
spareParts.tip: For turbo-DCT variants, always get the transmission oil changed at Hyundai-recommended intervals — it is a wet clutch design sensitive to fluid quality.

faqs.q: Is the turbo DCT reliable long-term?
faqs.a: Reliability has improved significantly since launch; sticking to Hyundai's recommended transmission fluid change interval is the biggest factor in long-term smoothness.

reviews.author: Meera Nair
reviews.title: Compact footprint, easy to drive in old city lanes
reviews.text: Perfect size for Kochi's narrower roads while still giving SUV stance and safety kit. Diesel option is getting harder to find on lower trims though.

spareParts.authorizedServiceNote: Shares its parts bin substantially with the i20 and Grand i10 Nios, keeping common part costs relatively low.
spareParts.tip: Because parts overlap with the i20, independent Hyundai-specialist garages outside the dealer network can often source them 15-20% cheaper.

faqs.q: Is the diesel Venue still available?
faqs.a: Diesel availability varies by trim and BS6 Phase 2 compliance updates — check current trim-wise availability with your local dealer before booking.
